implementation_constraints: reads one JSON object from stdin, exits 0/2, reason to stderr

unresolved_intent.decision: Fixed case-insensitive allowlist of tool names (read, view, glob, grep, ls, notebookread, webfetch, websearch) rather than inferring capability at runtime
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC names capabilities, not concrete tool identifiers; a host cannot report read-only-ness generically, so an explicit conservative allowlist is the only measurable signal

unresolved_intent.decision: A command is proven-reader only if it parses, contains no '>' redirection, and every stage's command basename is on a display/search allowlist (cat, head, tail, grep, rg, less, diff, ...); sed/awk/perl/tee/dd/cp/mv/rm and all interpreters are excluded
unresolved_intent.rationale: excluding editors and interpreters from the reader set makes writer-stage, in-place edit and tee fall to block without per-flag semantics

unresolved_intent.decision: Only '--in-place'/'--in-place=...' and any '>' redirection are write signals; generic '-i'/'-o' are NOT
unresolved_intent.rationale: '-i' (grep ignore-case) and '-o' (grep only-matching) are reader flags; a blanket flag block would falsely deny legitimate reads

unresolved_intent.ir_region: Shell tool identity and command extraction
unresolved_intent.decision: Case-insensitive shell/command tool-name set (bash, sh, zsh, cmd, powershell, pwsh, exec, run, terminal, ...); command read from tool_input['command']
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC says a shell tool carries the command under 'command' but does not name the tools; a missing/non-string command with a golden present blocks (fail-closed)

unresolved_intent.decision: Top-level JSON object with a string 'tool_name' and an object 'tool_input'; any other top-level or field type blocks
unresolved_intent.rationale: the two carried fields are the minimal contract every downstream rule depends on
